14835-the-burglar-and-the-blizzard-a-chr.title: The Burglar And The Blizzard A Christmas Story
14835-the-burglar-and-the-blizzard-a-chr.creator: Unknown
14835-the-burglar-and-the-blizzard-a-chr.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “Hillsborough, December 21st. The fourth in a series of daring robberies which have been taking place in this neighbourhood during the past month occurred last night when the residence of C. Vaughan of New York was entered and valuable wines and bric-a-brac removed. The robbery was not discovered until this morning when a shutter was observed unfastened on the second story.

arxiv-2012-02026.title: Towards an AI Assistant for Power Grid Operators
arxiv-2012-02026.creator: Antoine Marot, Alexandre Rozier, Matthieu Dussartre, Laure Crochepierre, Benjamin Donnot
arxiv-2012-02026.description: Abstract Power grids are becoming more complex to operate in the digital age given the current energy transition to cope with climate change. As a result, real-time decision-making is getting more challenging as the human operator has to deal with more information, more uncertainty, more applications, and more coordination.

arxiv-2106-13963.title: OffRoadTranSeg: Semi-Supervised Segmentation using Transformers on OffRoad environments
arxiv-2106-13963.creator: Anukriti Singh, Kartikeya Singh, P.B. Sujit
arxiv-2106-13963.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anukriti Singh, Kartikeya Singh, P.B. Sujit. We present OffRoadTranSeg, the first end-to-end framework for semi-supervised segmentation in unstructured outdoor environment using transformers and automatic data selection for labelling. The offroad segmentation is a scene understanding approach that is widely used in autonomous driving. The popular offroad segmentation method is to use fully connected convolution layers and large labelled data, however, due to class imbalance, there will be several mismatches and also some classes may not be detected.

arxiv-2112-11805.title: Neural-Symbolic Integration for Interactive Learning and Conceptual Grounding
arxiv-2112-11805.creator: Benedikt Wagner, Artur d’Avila Garcez
arxiv-2112-11805.description: Abstract We propose neural-symbolic integration for abstract concept explanation and interactive learning. Neural-symbolic integration and explanation allow users and domain-experts to learn about the data-driven decision making process of large neural models. The models are queried using a symbolic logic language.

arxiv-2203-09881.title: An Overview of Modest Models and Tools for Real Stochastic Timed Systems
arxiv-2203-09881.creator: Arnd Hartmanns
arxiv-2203-09881.description: Abstract We depend on the safe, reliable, and timely operation of cyber-physical systems ranging from smart grids to avionics components. Many of them involve time-dependent behaviours and are subject to randomness. Modelling languages and verification tools thus need to support these quantitative aspects.

arxiv-2210-11996.title: Unbalanced Triangle Detection and Enumeration Hardness for Unions of Conjunctive Queries
arxiv-2210-11996.creator: Karl Bringmann ORCID:0000-0003-1356-5177, Nofar Carmeli ORCID:0000-0003-0673-5510
arxiv-2210-11996.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Karl Bringmann ORCID:0000-0003-1356-5177, Nofar Carmeli ORCID:0000-0003-0673-5510. We study the enumeration of answers to Unions of Conjunctive Queries (UCQs) with optimal time guarantees. More precisely, we wish to identify the queries that can be solved with linear preprocessing time and constant delay.

arxiv-2308-14294.title: Implications of the electron-phonon coupling in CuPb 9 (PO 4 ) 6 O for superconductivity: an ab initio study
arxiv-2308-14294.creator: Hari Paudyal, Michael E. Flatté, Durga Paudyal
arxiv-2308-14294.description: Abstract We report a ​ b ​ i ​ n ​ i ​ t ​ i ​ o ab~initio calculations of the electronic and vibrational properties in CuPb 9 (PO 4 ) 6 O, including the electron-phonon coupling strength via strong-coupling Migdal-Eliashberg theory.

arxiv-2309-10642.title: CORRECTING SELECTION BIAS IN STANDARDIZED TEST COMPARISONS Thanks: Corresponding address: oib5044@psu.edu, Department of Economics, The Pennsylvania State University, University Park, PA 16802. I am grateful to Marc Henry, Andres Aradillas-Lopez, Michael Gechter, Ismael Mourifie, and all participant
arxiv-2309-10642.creator: Onil Boussim
arxiv-2309-10642.description: Abstract . This paper tackles the critical issue of sample selection bias in cross-country comparisons using international assessments such as PISA (Program for International Student Assessment). While PISA is widely used to rank educational performance, its reliance on samples of students still in school at age 15 introduces survival bias, potentially distorting comparisons.

arxiv-2311-09724.title: OVM , O utcome-supervised V alue M odels for Planning in Mathematical Reasoning
arxiv-2311-09724.creator: Fei Yu, Anningzhe Gao, Benyou WangThe Chinese Unviersity of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, ChinaShenzhen Research Institute of Big Data222043013@link.cuhk.edu.cn, gaoanningzhe@sribd.cn, wangbenyou@cuhk.edu.cn https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/OVM
arxiv-2311-09724.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) often struggle with maintaining accuracy throughout multiple multiple reasoning steps, especially in mathematical reasoning where an error in earlier steps can propagate to subsequent ones and it ultimately leading to an incorrect answer. To reduce error propagation, guided decoding is employed to direct the LM decoding on a step-by-step basis.

arxiv-2408-02953.title: Large Landscape of 4d Superconformal Field Theories from Small Gauge Theories
arxiv-2408-02953.creator: Minseok Cho, Kazunobu Maruyoshi, Emily Nardoni, and Jaewon Song
arxiv-2408-02953.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Minseok Cho, Kazunobu Maruyoshi, Emily Nardoni, and Jaewon Song. We systematically explore the space of renormalization group flows of four-dimensional 𝒩 = 1 {\cal N}=1 superconformal field theories (SCFTs) triggered by relevant deformations, as well as by coupling to free chiral multiplets with relevant operators.

arxiv-2409-13491.title: Closures and heavy pairs for hamiltonicity Thanks: Supported by NSFC (Nos. 12071370, 12171393, and 12131013), China Scholarship Council, P.R. China (No. 202206290004) and Shaanxi Fundamental Science Research Project for Mathematics and Physics (No. 22JSZ009).
arxiv-2409-13491.creator: Wangyi Shang, Hajo Broersma, Shenggui Zhang, Binlong Li
arxiv-2409-13491.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wangyi Shang, Hajo Broersma, Shenggui Zhang, Binlong Li. Abstract: We say that a graph G on n vertices is \{H,F\} - o -heavy if every induced subgraph of G isomorphic to H or F contains two nonadjacent vertices with degree sum at least n .

arxiv-2410-19617.title: Measurement-device-independent resource characterization protocols
arxiv-2410-19617.creator: Chenxu Li, Mingze Xu, Hao Dai, Xiongfeng Ma
arxiv-2410-19617.description: Abstract Measurement-device-independent (MDI) quantum information processing tasks are important subroutines in quantum information science because they are robust against any type of measurement imperfections. In this work, we propose a framework of MDI resource characterization protocols that unifies and generalizes these tasks.

arxiv-2410-20608.title: Contributions to the Algorithmic Foundations of Approximate Lie Symmetry Algebras of Differential Equations
arxiv-2410-20608.creator: Siyuan Deng, Gregory Reid
arxiv-2410-20608.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Siyuan Deng, Gregory Reid. Symmetry transformations that leave an object invariant, play a fundamental role in science and mathematics. In this article we consider Lie symmetry transformations, that depend analytically on their parameters, and leave the solution set of differential equations invariant. Such Lie symmetry groups uniquely determine their Lie symmetry algebras, which are the linearized form of the transformations near the identity transformation.

arxiv-2503-10747.title: Lévy Flights and Leaky Boxes: Anomalous Diffusion of Cosmic Rays
arxiv-2503-10747.creator: Naixin Liang, S. Peng Oh
arxiv-2503-10747.description: Abstract In classical diffusion, particle step-sizes have a Gaussian distribution. However, in superdiffusion, they have power-law tails, with transport dominated by rare, long ‘Lévy flights’. Similarly, if the time interval between scattering events has power-law tails, subdiffusion occurs. Both forms of anomalous diffusion are seen in cosmic ray (CR) particle tracking simulations in turbulent magnetic fields.

arxiv-2508-02527.title: I Have No Mouth, and I Must Rhyme: Uncovering Internal Phonetic Representations in LLaMA 3.2
arxiv-2508-02527.creator: Oliver McLaughlin, Arjun Khurana, Jack Merullo
arxiv-2508-02527.description: Abstract Large language models demonstrate proficiency on phonetic tasks, such as rhyming, without explicit phonetic or auditory grounding. In this work, we investigate how Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct represents token-level phonetic information. Our results suggest that Llama uses a rich internal model of phonemes to complete phonetic tasks. We provide evidence for high-level organization of phoneme representations in its latent space.

arxiv-2510-06793.title: Tuning pair interactions in colloidal systems using random light fields
arxiv-2510-06793.creator: Augustin Muster, Diego Romero Abujetas, Frank Scheffold, Luis S. Froufe-Pérez
arxiv-2510-06793.description: Abstract We propose a method to tune interactions between absorptionless colloidal particle pairs. This is achieved via optimization of the spectral energy density of a homogeneous random optical field. Several standard and more exotic interaction potentials, as well as their negative counterparts, are shown to be successfully tuned.

arxiv-2510-08805.title: Lifted Heston Model: Efficient Monte Carlo Simulation with Large Time Steps
arxiv-2510-08805.creator: NICOLA F. ZAUGG, LECH A. GRZELAK
arxiv-2510-08805.description: Abstract The lifted Heston model [ 1 ] is a stochastic volatility model emerging as a Markovian lift of the rough Heston model [ 13 ] and the class of rough volatility processes. The model encodes the path dependency of volatility on a set of N N square-root state processes driven by a common stochastic factor.

pmc-10622210.title: Coincidental occurrence of bilateral neonatal testicular torsion, with an extravaginal and a contralateral intravaginal testicular torsion
pmc-10622210.creator: Yusuke Kirihana, Yuichi Sato, Junya Hata, Hitomi Imai, Yuki Yoshida, Kanako Matsuoka, Seiji Hoshi, Tomoyuki Koguchi, Soichiro Ogawa, Yoshiyuki Kojima
pmc-10622210.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionWe report a case of bilateral neonatal testicular torsion, with an extravaginal and a contralateral intravaginal testicular torsion.Case presentationA 5‐day‐old boy with bilateral scrotal swelling and palpable induration was diagnosed with bilateral neonatal testicular torsion by color Doppler ultrasonography. The right testis was black with 360‐degree extravaginal torsion of the spermatic cord, and the left testis was brown with 90‐degree intravaginal torsion. We repaired the torsion and incised the tunica albuginea to reduce intratesticular pressure.

pmc-11289933.title: Prevalence of contraindicated combinations amid behavioral and mental health medications filled in a pediatric population
pmc-11289933.creator: Laura M Borgelt, Kathryn Bliss, Jacqueline Matson, Bosede Cajuste, Xiaoying Kuang, Monica Toohey, Wilson Pace, Eyal Shemesh, Suzanne Lo, Anna Olczyk, Kristine Gleason, Harold Pincus, Lawrence C Kleinman
pmc-11289933.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundBehavioral or mental health disorders are common in children, adolescents, and young adults. Medication use is increasingly common, with few data describing drug-drug combinations in ambulatory settings. The objectives of this study were to describe the pharmaco-epidemiology of behavioral and mental health (BMH) medications among children, adolescents, and young adults in New York Medicaid and assess the prevalence of contraindicated drug pairs within this population.MethodsThis observational cross-sectional study evaluated New York State Medicaid managed care and fee-for-service enrollees under 21 years of

pmc-11438683.title: Global strategy for prevention of gastric cancer
pmc-11438683.creator: Sergey M Kotelevets
pmc-11438683.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Global prevention of gastric cancer needs to increase its level of effectiveness. The prevention strategy should include all stages of primary and secondary prevention. The necessary steps to prevent gastric cancer are the following: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle and diet, avoiding smoking and alcohol; serological screening of Helicobacter pylori infections and eradication; serological screening of atrophic gastritis in the population over 45 years of age and identification of severe atrophic gastritis with a high risk of developing gastric cancer; verification of atrophic

pmc-11739270.title: Investigation of the Effect of Mobile and Immobile Regions on Fat Graft Viability: An Experimental Study in a New Model
pmc-11739270.creator: Gökçen Çakır Bozkurt, Levent Yoleri, Peyker Temiz
pmc-11739270.description: BackgroundFat grafts are widely used in plastic, aesthetic and reconstructive surgery. Their unpredictable resorption is their main disadvantage. A review of the literature shows that there is a lack of research on the effect of mobile and immobile regions on fat graft survival in fat graft applications.

pmc-12573057.title: Debate: Social media in children and young people – time for a ban? Beyond bans: addressing the digital determinants of youth mental health and well‐being in the European region
pmc-12573057.creator: Cassie Redlich, Ledia Lazeri, Jason Maurer, Jennifer Hall, Natasha Azzopardi‐Muscat
pmc-12573057.description: The complex role that social media plays in shaping young people's mental health and well‐being requires a nuanced approach to regulation beyond simple bans. Social media presents demonstrated harms for young people, yet can also be a lifeline and provide a valuable resource for social support, learning, and expression.

pmc-12992773.title: A high-resolution spatiotemporal wildfire propagation dataset for the Mediterranean and Europe
pmc-12992773.creator: Simon Müller, Anja Hofmann-Böllinghaus, Zhimin Chen, Kristin Vogel, Philipp Benner
pmc-12992773.description: Wildfires are becoming more frequent and severe under the influence of climate change, posing increasing risks to ecosystems, human health, and infrastructure. Accurate spatiotemporal data on wildfire propagation is essential for advancing fire behavior modeling, improving management strategies, and mitigating future impacts. However, existing datasets with both high spatial and temporal resolution are rare, costly, and time-consuming to produce.

pmc-13349217.title: Growth-Friendly Surgery Improves Diaphragm Positioning, Thoracic Dimensions, and Patient-Reported Outcomes in Neuromuscular Scoliosis
pmc-13349217.creator: Zaid Elsabbagh, William ElNemer, Peter G. Gabos, Gregory J. Redding, Paul D. Sponseller
pmc-13349217.description: Background:Neuromuscular scoliosis (NMS) can displace the diaphragm into the thorax, reducing lung volume and impairing respiration. As an alternative to posterior spinal fusion, growth-friendly surgery (GFS) allows thoracic growth while correcting deformity. We evaluated associations of GFS with thoracic dimensions and diaphragm positioning, hypothesizing that GFS would alleviate respiratory constraints in pediatric NMS.

pmc-13356833.title: Comparative Analysis of Corneal Endothelial Cell Loss After Phacoemulsification in Microcornea versus Normal-Sized Corneas
pmc-13356833.creator: Tianyu Zheng, Peimin Lin, Ao Miao, Yating Tang, Yongxiang Jiang, Jie Xu
pmc-13356833.description: BackgroundPhacoemulsification is inevitably accompanied by loss of corneal endothelial cells, and microcornea eyes with crowded anterior segments may be more susceptible to this damage.PurposeThis study aimed to compare endothelial cell loss (ECL) after cataract phacoemulsification surgery between eyes with microcornea and those with normal-sized corneas.

pmc-13392262.title: Mevalonate pathway rewiring driven by enhancer remodelling confers resistance to KRAS inhibitors in colorectal cancer
pmc-13392262.creator: Yaoyu Guo, Yi Zhong, Peishan Hu, Yufeng Chen, Wenjun Guo, Jianfeng Chen, Peiyong Guan, Zhengran Zhou, Fang Zhu, Xian Zeng, Jiuping Gao, Qiqing Xiong, Zhaoliang Yu, Chuling Hu, Zerong Cai, Xiaoyu Xie, Jing Han Hong, Jason Yongsheng Chan, Wenyu Wang, Dechang Diao, Xiaojun Xia, Qiang Yu, Choon Kiat Ong
pmc-13392262.description: KRAS inhibitors (KRASi) have emerged as promising new cancer therapeutics for KRAS-mutant cancers; however, resistance remains a potential clinical challenge. Here, we show that reactivation of ERK is a hallmark of KRASi-resistant colorectal cancers (CRCs) and further demonstrate that enhancer remodeling rewires cholesterol biosynthesis through the mevalonate (MVA) pathway to confer this resistance.
